title: The same identification for Jansenius and Estius
source_text: LVIII. Eodem modo gratia excitans eadem est cum operante, & gratia adjuvans eadem cum cooperante, omnibus illis, qui cum Jansenio & Estio per gratiam excitantem intelligunt illam, quae revera excitat peccatorem a somno peccati, & per adjuvantem illam qua homo adjuvatur, ut perficiat bonum quod jam velle incepit: Ac per operantem eam quae in nobis efficit primum conversionis actum, per cooperantem eam quae alios sequentes, ad quos non tantum libero quodam voluntatis influxu, sed etiam praevio aliquo studio & conatu nostro cooperamur.
pass_a_gloss: LVIII. In the same way rousing grace is the same as operating, and helping grace the same as cooperating, for all those, who with Jansenius and Estius by rousing grace understand that, which really rouses the sinner from the sleep of sin, and by helping that by which man is helped, that he may perfect the good which he has already begun to will: And by operating that which effects in us the first act of conversion, by cooperating that which effects the others following, to which we cooperate not only by a certain free influx of the will, but also by some previous effort and striving of ours.
pass_b_english: Thesis LVIII. Rousing grace is likewise the same as operating grace, and assisting grace the same as cooperating grace, for all who, with Jansenius and Estius, take rousing grace to be the grace that actually wakes the sinner from the sleep of sin, and assisting grace the grace by which a person is helped to complete the good he has already begun to will.

They also take operating grace to be the grace that produces in us the first act of conversion, and cooperating grace the grace that produces the acts that follow, in which we cooperate not only by a free contribution of the will but also by some prior effort and striving of our own.

choices.why: The scholastic pair: grace that rouses and calls, and grace that helps the will to will and to act; kept as in the previous packet.
